And Award All Statutory Benefits And Grant Any

 This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The appellant being the owner of land bearing Sy.No.112 of Deginal village, Indi Taluk, Vijayapur District, which was proposed to be acquired in terms of the notification dated 28.06.2007 under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, for the purpose of construction of Minor Irrigation Tank (Jeenugu Kere Canal) has filed this appeal challenging the judgment and award passed by the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Indi (henceforth referred as 'Reference Court') dated 21.04.2014 in LAC No.44/2012.
2.
The aforesaid land was acquired for the purpose stated above.
The Land Acquisition Officer passed an award on 06.01.2009 awarding a sum of Rs.33,076/- per acre as the compensation in respect of wet land.
The appellant sought enhancement of compensation which was referred under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The Reference Court after considering the oral and documentary evidence, relied upon a judgment of this Court in MFA No.2020/2005 and enhanced the compensation to a sum of Rs.3,00,800/- per acre.
Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and award passed by the Reference Court, the present appeal is filed.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the judgment in MFA No.2020/2005 was not in respect of the land situate in Deginal village, but was in respect of Bommanajogi village in Sindagi Taluk.

He further submitted that the notification in the present case was issued on 28.06.2007,
while the notification in MFA No.2020/2005 was issued on 08.01.1996.
Therefore, he contended that the judgment of the Reference Court is not based on the merits of the case.

He submitted that this Court in MFA No.200063/2017 and connected matters had in similar circumstances,
considered the above and had set aside the order passed by the Reference Court in respect of acquisition of lands in Sy.Nos.93/2, 93/3, 93/1A and 93/1B of Deginal village.
He therefore, submits that this appeal may also be remitted back before the Reference Court for re-consideration by the Reference Court in accordance with law.
4. Learned High Court Government Pleader does not dispute the aforesaid.
